items.claim: The opening superscription unit is byte-warranted at both ends and its quote tier, Masoretic-mark, and disclosure handling are clean.
items.evidence: The title splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.1.1, and the three-reign dating argued in the span (thirteenth year of Josiah, the Jehoiakim stretch, the eleventh year of Zedekiah and the fifth-month deportation) stands in the bytes of oshb:Jer.1.2 and oshb:Jer.1.3. The unit's own close is correctly warranted by content rather than by a blended sweep: the third verse itself opens with the bare narrative connector וַיְהִ֗י (oshb:Jer.1.3, byte tier), and the row is careful to name the full three-word word-event shape וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.1.4, byte tier) as the thing that begins outside this span — the shape whose census is 21 verses book-wide, the first four sites all falling in these two chapters. Disclosure is complete for the span: one setumah at oshb:Jer.1.3, typed correctly, cited single-witness at weak tier and not made a driver; the ketiv/qere and paseq inventories are both empty across these three verses, so nothing further is owed. No cross-tradition material, no fabrication class, and no numbering-zone exposure — the span is far from the book's single offset zone and from its one non-Hebrew verse.

items.claim: A ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed, and the rescue-formula recurrence the row builds on is asserted with neither a tier label nor a book-wide digit.
items.evidence: One of the book's 141 ketiv/qere notes (over 124 verses) falls inside this span, at oshb:Jer.1.5, and the doublet is plainly visible in the bytes as אצורך אֶצָּרְךָ֤ — an unpointed ketiv standing beside its pointed qere (oshb:Jer.1.5, byte tier). The row argues that verse's appointment content while disclosing only the segment-mark layer, so the largest ketiv/qere inventory in this book is silently passed over in a verse the row reads. Second, the rescue-formula claim is offered as a bracket around the call and both vision reports but carries no tier and no digit. The element that is genuinely byte-identical at the two sites is כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier), and a byte-tier sweep of that run returns 4 verses book-wide (oshb:Jer.1.8, oshb:Jer.1.19, oshb:Jer.15.20, oshb:Jer.30.11), so the bracket is real but is not distinctive to this chapter; the rescue infinitives themselves differ in spelling between the two verses, defective at the earlier site and plene at the later one, which is why the row's hedge to close wording is right and its lack of a tier is not. Everything else in the row is byte-sound: the onset splice re-collates at byte tier as the first of the 21 word-event sites; the divine-title stack אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.1.6, byte tier) is quoted, named, and is indeed one of the qamats divine-title sites among the 13 bare adonai-token verses rather than a courtly address; and both petuchah segments in the span are typed correctly, placed correctly, and tier-disclosed.

items.claim: The two-verse vision unit is byte-warranted at both ends, its pun engagement is byte-true and correctly kept apart from the lookalike keyword, and its disclosure is exact.
items.evidence: Both splices re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.1.11 and oshb:Jer.1.12. The pun pair stands in the bytes of the two verses as מַקֵּ֥ל שָׁקֵ֖ד (oshb:Jer.1.11, byte tier) against שֹׁקֵ֥ד (oshb:Jer.1.12, byte tier), and the row names the pun by its own form instead of counting it against the falsehood keyword — the exact discipline the two-letter overlap demands, and it declines to attach a digit precisely because it is not counting. The onset claim matches the frame census: this is the second of the 21 word-event sites, and the row reports the following verse's own ordinal word שֵׁנִ֣ית (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier) as the text's wording without letting it collide with the token order — it says both that this is the third formula token and that the text calls it a second time, which is the byte-true reading of the pair. Disclosure is complete: the petuchah before the span and the petuchah at its close are typed correctly and bracket the span exactly, the first verse carries no mark, and the ketiv/qere and paseq inventories are empty inside the span.

items.claim: An unbroken divine speech runs across the row's own close undisclosed, the close warrant rests on a form label the pointed bytes do not carry, and the motif claims are anchored on the wrong verse without a sweep digit.
items.evidence: The speech this span sits in is opened by the narrative frame verb וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier) and continues past the row's close to the end of the chapter with no further speech introduction: the verses after the close carry no fresh frame verb, no word-event formula (the next of the 21 sites lies far outside this chapter), and no change of speaker or addressee — YHWH to the prophet throughout. That is a byte-true continuity straddling the row's own seam, and it is undisclosed, while the same criterion the row uses to keep its interpretation verses inside the unit (no fresh formula, imperative, or addressee) would equally keep the following three verses inside it. The named close warrant is a second-person charge marked by an imperative construction, but the cited form is וְאַתָּה֙ תֶּאְזֹ֣ר (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier): a taw-prefixed prefix conjugation after an emphatic pronoun, not the plain imperative shape this book uses for its discourse frames (שִׁמְע֥וּ at oshb:Jer.2.4 and רְא֣וּ at oshb:Jer.2.31, byte tier). No morphology layer is staged, so this is held on the pointed bytes plus both renderings: the second witness does render it as a command (“You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise” web:Jer.1.17), so the force is imperatival and the form label is functional — which the row does not say. Finally, the northern-invader motif is said to be introduced at the span's third verse, but its first site in the book is the span's own opening verse, צָפֽוֹנָה (oshb:Jer.1.13, byte tier); a skeleton sweep of that spelling returns 5 verses book-wide and the contiguous northern skeleton returns 20, while the phrase actually unique to the third verse is a different object (skeleton sweep: 1 verse). Neither the introduction claim nor the recurs-across-the-book claim carries a digit or a tier, and the scope phrase covering the remaining northern material is not verse-anchored. Mark handling is correct: no segment mark inside the span, the preceding petuchah typed and placed correctly, and no ketiv/qere note in the span.

items.claim: The row's own stated boundary warrant, that its closing clause is the same rescue clause as the earlier one, is contested at byte level, and the span continues a divine speech opened three verses before its onset without disclosure.
items.evidence: The two clauses are not the same. The shared element כִּֽי אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier) is byte-identical with the earlier site, but a byte-tier sweep of that run returns 4 verses book-wide (oshb:Jer.1.8, oshb:Jer.1.19, oshb:Jer.15.20, oshb:Jer.30.11), so it does not single out this chapter; the rescue infinitive differs in spelling between the two verses, defective לְהַצִּלֶ֖ךָ (oshb:Jer.1.8, byte tier; skeleton sweep: 1 verse book-wide) against plene לְהַצִּילֶֽךָ (oshb:Jer.1.19, byte tier; skeleton sweep: 2 verses, the other outside this part); and the postpositive formula stands after the infinitive in the earlier verse and before it in the later one. Mater-lectionis pairs are live in this book, so an identity claim here needs either a re-cut to the byte-identical core or a tier label, and the row carries neither while resting its fresh-unit case on this bracket. Second, the span opens no speech of its own: it continues the divine speech begun at וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.1.14, byte tier), and its onset verse adds no formula and no change of speaker or addressee — an undisclosed cross-seam continuity, though the row does honestly record that its onset carries no word-event formula. Third, gloss extent misses splice extent in both directions: the four-word closing splice is glossed by two English words, and the three-word onset splice is glossed by a rendering that reaches into the following clause (“You therefore put your belt on your waist, arise” web:Jer.1.17, where the last word renders וְקַמְתָּ֙ (oshb:Jer.1.17, byte tier), outside the spliced run). The unit type is narrative prose over a span carrying no narrative verb at all — every verse is inside the quoted divine speech. The row's declared heuristic false positive, an evidence ref for the call-narrative onset verse that the prose does not name in so many words, is CONFIRMED as a false positive: the prose argues the call narrative as the bracketed material and the ref is that narrative's own onset, so the listing errs toward over-listing, which is the safe direction. Mark handling is correct: the closing petuchah is typed and placed correctly and the span carries no ketiv/qere note.

items.claim: The row asserts a go-and-proclaim frame and carries a substrate signal for it but never quotes that form, and the splice it does give starts after the frame and stops inside a construct chain that its gloss then completes.
items.evidence: The asserted frame sits in the cited verse's bytes as הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier; skeleton sweep of that pair: 2 verses book-wide, the other outside this part), but the row's splice begins three words later at the messenger formula, so the frame form the row names and signals is never shown — a frame claim without its own quoted form. The pointed shape of the head word is the infinitive-absolute one followed by a waw-prefixed perfect, not a plain imperative; no morphology layer is staged, so this is held on the pointed bytes plus both renderings, and the second witness does render the pair as a command (“Go and proclaim in the ears of Jerusalem” web:Jer.2.2) — the label is functional, and the row does not mark it as such. The splice then ends on the construct אַהֲבַ֖ת (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier) while the gloss supplied for it needs the following word כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.2, byte tier), which lies outside the splice, and the messenger formula inside the splice is left unglossed: extent misses in both directions. The rest is byte-clean and well handled: the onset splice re-collates at byte tier as the fourth of the 21 word-event sites; the messenger formula's mouth is named as divine, which is the discipline this book's formula requires; the closing postpositive formula stands in the bytes of oshb:Jer.2.3; both petuchah segments are typed and placed correctly; and the span carries no ketiv/qere note.

items.claim: The row's internal-cohesion warrant, that no fresh imperative or formula intervenes before its close, is refuted by the messenger formula standing verse-initially in the span's second verse and by the imperative chains in two verses the row itself cites as evidence.
items.evidence: כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה stands verse-initially at oshb:Jer.2.5 (byte tier), inside the span; a skeleton sweep of the messenger formula returns exactly 2 verses in this chapter, the row's preceding-unit verse and this one, against a book-wide census of 153 verses. Its mouth is divine, relayed by the prophet after the summons, so no frame-owner change accompanies it — which is precisely the disposition the row needed to state under this book's cut rule; instead it denied the formula outright. Two verses the row cites as its own witness-summons evidence are imperative chains: עִבְר֞וּ and וּרְא֔וּ and שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ at oshb:Jer.2.10, and שֹׁ֥מּוּ with וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ at oshb:Jer.2.12 (byte tier), rendered as commands in the second witness as well (“For pass over to the islands of Kittim, and see.” web:Jer.2.10; “Be astonished, you heavens, at this and be horribly afraid.” web:Jer.2.12). The universal negative is therefore contradicted from inside the row's own evidence set, and it is the sentence carrying the unit's cohesion. The boundary itself survives on other grounds and the rest of the row is byte-sound: the onset summons שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.2.4, byte tier) is verse-initial and correctly quoted; the contention verb at oshb:Jer.2.9 and the two-evils close at oshb:Jer.2.13 sit in the cited bytes; the span carries no ketiv/qere note; and the segment-mark inventory is genuinely silent inside it, with the preceding petuchah typed correctly.

items.claim: Six of the book's ketiv/qere verses fall inside this span undisclosed, two of them under the very clauses the row glosses, and the row's blanket denial of any discourse imperative or addressee shift is refuted by the bytes at the same verse where its own disclosed segment mark falls.
items.evidence: Six of the 124 ketiv/qere verses (six of the 141 notes) sit inside this span and none is disclosed. Two carry the clauses the row argues from: the wild-donkey verse holds נפשו נַפְשָׁהּ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.24, byte tier), an unpointed ketiv beside a pointed qere whose suffix is exactly what the row's feminine reading depends on, and the idol-address verse holds ילדתני יְלִדְתָּ֔נוּ (oshb:Jer.2.27, byte tier), where the two readings differ in the person and number the row glosses. Glossing inside a ketiv/qere verse without the note is the hazard this book's largest inventory exists to prevent. Next, the blanket denial fails on two of its four terms. Discourse imperatives stand at וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ (oshb:Jer.2.19), רְאִ֤י דַרְכֵּךְ֙ and דְּעִ֖י (oshb:Jer.2.23), and מִנְעִ֤י רַגְלֵךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.2.25), all byte tier and all rendered as commands in the second witness (“Know therefore and see” web:Jer.2.19; “See your way in the valley. Know what you have done.” web:Jer.2.23; “Keep your feet from being bare, and your throat from thirst.” web:Jer.2.25). The addressee changes twice inside the span: from the feminine singular of עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Jer.2.17) to the masculine singular of וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔ךְ closing on the vocative יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.2.28), then to the plural of כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם (oshb:Jer.2.29) and חַרְבְּכֶ֛ם נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.2.30), all byte tier and all carried in the second witness too (“you have as many gods as you have towns, O Judah” web:Jer.2.28; “You all have transgressed against me” web:Jer.2.29). The first of those shifts falls at the setumah the row disclosed and then dismissed as accompanied by no formula or imperative — a participant shift at that seam is a candidate internal boundary the row never weighs, in a span it already holds at reduced confidence for its length. The other two terms of the denial do hold: the next word-event site lies far outside this chapter and the chapter's only two messenger-formula verses both fall outside this span. Finally the title-stack claim blends two distinct objects and quotes neither: the bytes give נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת at oshb:Jer.2.19 but נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה without the hosts element at oshb:Jer.2.22 (byte tier); skeleton sweeps return 3 verses book-wide for the longer stack and 4 for the shorter, so the second site is the lone member of the four-site stack object lacking that element. The row names one parenthesised form for both sites, drops the postpositive element that makes the shape a closure formula at all, and supplies no pointed splice for either. Mark handling itself is correct: the setumah is the only segment mark in the span, typed and tier-disclosed properly.
